ko: 1980년 가난한 셋방, 처음으로 뒤집기에 성공했습니다. 어머니가 손뼉을 치며 좋아합니다.
mt: In 1980, the poor rented room, which was the first time it was turned upside down, and my mother clapped her hands and loved it.
en: 1980, a cramped rented room. You roll over for the first time. Your mother claps her hands in delight.

ko: 1981년 겨울밤, 배가 고파 눈을 떴습니다. 방 안에는 연탄 냄새가 희미하게 떠돕니다.
mt: On the winter night of 1981, I was hungry, and inside the room, there was a faint smell of lotus gas.
en: A winter night in 1981. Hunger wakes you. The faint smell of coal briquettes hangs in the room.

ko: 집에 낯선 손님이 찾아와 당신을 안아 듭니다. 새로 들인 컬러텔레비전 소리가 시끄럽습니다.
mt: A stranger comes home and hugs you. The sound of new color television is noisy.
en: A stranger visits and picks you up. The new color television is loud.

mt: The stone-fishing table is set up. What do you want to catch?
en: The first-birthday table is set. What will you grab?

ko: 첫 걸음마를 떼려 합니다. 마루는 반질반질 윤이 납니다.
mt: I'm going to take off my first steps. The floor is shiny.
en: You are about to take your first steps. The wooden floor is polished to a shine.

ko: 아빠가 낡은 자장가를 불러 줍니다. 라디오에서는 뉴스가 흘러나옵니다.
mt: My dad sings an old lullaby, and the news comes out on the radio.
en: Your father sings an old lullaby. The news murmurs from the radio.

ko: 열이 펄펄 끓는 밤입니다. 방 안에는 물수건 냄새가 가득합니다.
mt: It's a hot, boiling night, and the inside of the room is full of water towels.
en: A night of burning fever. The room smells of damp washcloths.

ko: 형이 장난감 자동차를 빼앗아 갔습니다. 방바닥에는 낡은 양철 인형이 굴러다닙니다.
mt: He took his toy car, and there's an old tin doll on the floor.
en: Your older brother snatches your toy car. A battered tin doll rolls across the floor.

ko: 할머니가 당신의 작은 손을 펼쳐 손금을 들여다봅니다. 마당에는 빨래가 널려 있습니다.
mt: Grandma opens your little hand and looks into the palm of your hand, and there's a lot of laundry in the yard.
en: Your grandmother opens your little hand and studies your palm. Laundry hangs in the yard.

ko: 처음으로 말을 하려 입을 뗍니다. 아홉 시 뉴스를 알리는 시보가 방 안에 울립니다.
mt: And for the first time, she's going to talk, and she's going to ring in the room, telling me the news at nine o'clock.
en: You open your mouth to speak for the first time. The chime for the nine o'clock news rings through the room.

ko: 이유식을 처음 먹어 봅니다. 알루미늄 그릇에는 미음이 담겨 있습니다.
mt: I'm going to try this first, and I'm going to try it for the first time.
en: You taste baby food for the first time. Thin rice gruel fills an aluminum bowl.

ko: 부모가 다투는 소리에 잠이 깼습니다. 방문 너머로 술 냄새가 스며듭니다.
mt: I was awakened by my parents' argument, and I smelled the alcohol after the visit.
en: Your parents' quarreling wakes you. The smell of liquor seeps under the door.

ko: 골목 어귀 교회에서 종소리가 들려옵니다. 집 앞 골목에는 연탄 리어카가 지나갑니다.
mt: There's a bell coming from a church in the alley, and in the alley in front of the house, there's a flare car.
en: Church bells ring from the end of the alley. A coal-briquette cart rattles past the house.

ko: 셋방 집주인이 집세를 받으러 찾아왔습니다. 방 안에는 외상값 장부가 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: The owner of the rented room came to collect the rent, and there's a credit card in the room.
en: The landlord comes to collect the rent. A ledger of unpaid tabs lies open in the room.

ko: 여름, 동네 개울에서 처음으로 물놀이를 합니다. 물이 차갑고 맑습니다.
mt: In the summer, we play water for the first time in the local stream, and the water is cold and clear.
en: Summer. You splash in the neighborhood stream for the first time. The water is cold and clear.

ko: 동네 아이가 사탕을 내밉니다. 은박지에 싸인 사탕입니다.
mt: A kid in the neighborhood puts out candy, and it's wrapped in a silver jacket.
en: A neighborhood kid holds out a candy wrapped in foil.

ko: 길을 가던 노승이 당신을 보고 멈춰 섭니다. 흙먼지 날리는 비포장 골목입니다.
mt: The roadman stops to see you, and you're in a dirty, unpaved alley.
en: An old monk passing by stops when he sees you. Dust blows down the unpaved alley.

ko: 장난감 블록을 쌓고 있습니다. 바닥에는 시장에서 산 플라스틱 블록과 나무 블록이 섞여 있습니다.
mt: On the bottom, there's a mixture of plastic and wood blocks from the market.
en: You are stacking toy blocks. Plastic blocks from the market are mixed with wooden ones on the floor.

ko: 아버지가 주택복권 몇 장을 사 와 당신에게 한 장을 골라 달라고 합니다. 텔레비전에서는 추첨 방송이 흘러나옵니다.
mt: My dad buys a few house tickets and asks you to pick one, and television shows show show off.
en: Your father brings home some housing lottery tickets and asks you to pick one. The draw is playing on TV.

ko: 어머니가 당신을 업고 시장에 장을 보러 갑니다. 생선 가게에서 비린내가 납니다.
mt: My mother carries you up to the market to go shopping, and the fish store is empty.
en: Your mother carries you on her back to the market. The fish stall reeks.

ko: 중동 건설 현장에 나간 삼촌이 큰 선물 상자를 보내왔습니다. 상자에는 외국 우표가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: My uncle came out of the construction site in the Middle East and he sent me a big gift box with foreign stamps on it.
en: Your uncle, working construction in the Middle East, sends a big gift box covered in foreign stamps.

ko: 동생이 태어났습니다. 병원에서 돌아온 어머니 품에는 작은 포대기가 안겨 있습니다.
mt: My brother was born, and my mother came back from the hospital, and she has a little pretzel in her arms.
en: A younger sibling is born. Your mother comes home from the hospital cradling a tiny bundle.

ko: 처음으로 거울 속의 자신을 발견했습니다. 낡은 장롱에 붙은 거울입니다.
mt: For the first time, I found myself in a mirror, a mirror attached to an old road.
en: You discover yourself in a mirror for the first time, the one on the old wardrobe.

ko: 큰 천둥이 치는 밤입니다. 전기가 나가 촛불만 깜빡입니다.
mt: It's a night of thunder and thunder. The power goes out and the candle goes off.
en: A night of loud thunder. The power is out, and only a candle flickers.

ko: 두 살 생일 케이크 앞입니다. 방 안에는 흰 양초가 켜져 있습니다.
mt: It's in front of a two-year-old birthday cake with white candles on in the room.
en: You sit before your second birthday cake. White candles glow in the room.

ko: 1985년 유치원 첫날입니다. 교실 한쪽에는 낡은 풍금이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: It's the first day of kindergarten in 1985, and on one side of the classroom is an old fan.
en: 1985, your first day of kindergarten. An old pump organ stands in the corner of the classroom.

ko: 친구가 놀이터에서 넘어져 무릎이 까졌습니다. 흙바닥에 빨간 피가 맺힙니다.
mt: A friend of mine fell down on the playground and broke his knee, and he had red blood on the dirt floor.
en: A friend falls on the playground and scrapes a knee. Red blood beads on the dirt.

ko: 산타 할아버지에게 편지를 씁니다. 크레파스로 쓴 글씨가 삐뚤빼뚤합니다.
mt: I write a letter to Santa Claus, and it's a little bit of a pre-fabricated letter.
en: You write a letter to Santa. Your crayon letters wobble across the page.

ko: 주일학교 선생님이 성경 이야기를 들려줍니다. 낡은 환풍기가 돌아갑니다.
mt: The Sunday school teacher tells me a story about the Bible, and the old fan turns.
en: The Sunday school teacher tells a Bible story. An old ventilation fan whirs.

ko: 놀이터 미끄럼틀 앞에 아이들이 줄을 서 있습니다.
mt: There's a line of kids in front of the playground slide.
en: Children are lined up at the playground slide.

ko: 엄마가 시장에서 사탕 하나를 골라도 된다고 합니다. 진열대에는 알록달록한 봉지 과자가 가득합니다.
mt: Mom says you can pick a candy from the market, and the shelves are full of aluminum bags.
en: Mom says you can pick one candy at the market. The shelves are packed with colorful bags of snacks.

ko: 아빠와 함께 자전거 타기를 배웁니다. 골목길 끝에는 낡은 전봇대가 서 있습니다.
mt: I learn to ride my bike with my dad, and at the end of the alley, there's an old poles.
en: Your father teaches you to ride a bike. An old utility pole stands at the end of the alley.

ko: 유치원 학예회에서 역할을 맡게 되었습니다. 무대 천막에는 색종이 장식이 달려 있습니다.
mt: I was assigned to the kindergarten trial, and there's colored paper in the tent.
en: You get a part in the kindergarten play. Paper decorations hang from the stage tent.

ko: 친구네 집이 무척 커서 놀랐습니다. 대문 앞에 자가용이 세워져 있습니다.
mt: His house is very large, and I'm surprised, and I'm standing in front of the gate with a self-sharing machine.
en: Your friend's house is huge, and it startles you. A private car is parked by the gate.

ko: 길에서 동전 하나를 주웠습니다. 바닥에는 비가 고인 웅덩이가 있습니다.
mt: I picked up a coin on the street. There's a rainy pool on the floor.
en: You find a coin on the street, next to a rain puddle.

ko: 할아버지가 바둑을 가르쳐 줍니다. 낡은 장판 위에 바둑판이 펼쳐집니다.
mt: My grandfather teaches me the GO, and it's spread out on the old shelf.
en: Your grandfather teaches you baduk. The board is laid out on the worn linoleum.

ko: 감기에 걸려 유치원을 쉬게 되었습니다. 방에는 뜨거운 약탕기 냄새가 납니다.
mt: I get a cold, I get a kindergarten break, and in the room I smell like hot medicine.
en: You catch a cold and stay home from kindergarten. The room smells of a bubbling herbal medicine pot.

ko: 과천에 새로 생긴 서울대공원 동물원에 갔습니다. 우리 안 사자가 하품을 합니다.
mt: I went to the new Seoul Park Zoo in Guang, where a lion yawns inside of us.
en: You visit the new Seoul Grand Park Zoo in Gwacheon. A lion yawns in its enclosure.

ko: 친구가 당신의 그림을 보고 비웃습니다. 교실에는 크레파스 냄새가 납니다.
mt: A friend of yours laughs at your painting.
en: A friend laughs at your drawing. The classroom smells of crayons.

ko: 성당에서 처음으로 미사에 참석했습니다. 스테인드글라스가 햇살을 받아 빛납니다.
mt: I attended Mass for the first time in the church, and the stained glass shines in the sun.
en: You attend Mass for the first time. Stained glass glows in the sunlight.

ko: 부모님이 용돈 기입장을 주었습니다. 표지에는 로보트 태권브이가 그려져 있습니다.
mt: My parents gave me a quick ride, and on the cover, I have a robot tape.
en: Your parents give you an allowance ledger. Robot Taekwon V is printed on the cover.

ko: 낯선 어른이 사탕을 줄 테니 따라오라고 합니다. 골목 어귀에는 아무도 없습니다.
mt: There's no one in the alley.
en: A strange adult says to follow him for some candy. No one is at the mouth of the alley.

ko: 동네 형들이 축구에 끼워 줍니다. 공터에는 돌멩이로 만든 골대가 있습니다.
mt: The local brothers join us in football, and there's a rock frame in the open.
en: The neighborhood big kids let you join their soccer game. The goalposts in the empty lot are made of stones.

ko: 밤에 혼자 화장실에 가야 합니다. 복도 끝 전구가 깜빡입니다.
mt: I have to go to the bathroom by myself at night. I'm blinking at the end of the hall.
en: You have to go to the bathroom alone at night. The bulb at the end of the hall flickers.

ko: 엄마 화장대에서 립스틱을 발견했습니다. 화장대 위에는 분첩과 향수병이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: I found lipstick on my mother's calisthenic table, and on top of it, there's chalk and perfume bottles.
en: You find a lipstick on Mom's vanity, among a powder compact and perfume bottles.

ko: 이웃 할머니가 혼자 무거운 짐을 들고 골목을 올라갑니다.
mt: The neighbor goes up the alley alone with a heavy load.
en: An elderly neighbor is hauling a heavy load up the alley alone.

ko: 유치원 선생님이 장래 희망을 묻습니다. 칠판에는 동물 그림이 그려져 있습니다.
mt: The kindergarten teacher asks us about hope for the future, and there's an animal painting on the blackboard.
en: The kindergarten teacher asks what you want to be. Animals are drawn on the blackboard.

ko: 동생과 과자를 나눠 먹어야 합니다. 과자 봉지에는 바삭한 쌀과자가 들어 있습니다.
mt: You've got to divide your brother's and your snacks. There's fresh rice in the bag.
en: You have to share snacks with your younger sibling. The bag is full of crunchy rice crackers.

ko: 유치원에서 도둑 누명을 썼습니다. 없어진 것은 선생님의 지갑입니다.
mt: I used a thief's name in kindergarten. What's missing is your wallet.
en: You are falsely accused of theft at kindergarten. What went missing is the teacher's wallet.

ko: 아빠가 일자리를 잃었습니다. 집안이 조용하고 밥상도 초라합니다.
mt: Dad lost his job. The house is quiet and the table is humble.
en: Your father loses his job. The house is quiet, and the meals are meager.

ko: 친척 결혼식에 갔습니다. 예식장에는 하얀 드레스와 꽃 장식이 가득합니다.
mt: I went to a relative's wedding, and the wedding hall is full of white dresses and flower decorations.
en: You attend a relative's wedding. The hall is full of white gowns and flowers.

ko: 개울가에서 친구들과 물고기를 잡습니다. 물살이 제법 세고 차갑습니다.
mt: I catch fish with my friends by the stream, and the water is fine and cold.
en: You catch fish in the stream with friends. The current is strong and cold.

ko: 동네 점쟁이 할머니가 당신을 불러 세웁니다. 할머니 앞에는 부채와 쌀이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: The local fortune-teller calls you up, and there's debt and rice in front of her.
en: The neighborhood fortune-teller calls you over. A fan and a dish of rice sit before her.

ko: 한글을 배우기 시작했습니다. 골목 간판마다 글자가 가득합니다.
mt: I started to learn Hankul. Every street sign is full of letters.
en: You begin learning Hangul. Every sign in the alley is full of letters.

ko: 생일 파티에 반 친구들을 초대합니다. 식탁에는 생일 케이크가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: I invite my classmates to a birthday party, and there's a birthday cake on the table.
en: You invite your classmates to a birthday party. A birthday cake sits on the table.

ko: 텔레비전에서 큰 지진 소식이 나옵니다. 화면에는 무너진 건물과 구호 천막이 보입니다.
mt: On television, we're talking about a big earthquake, and on the screen, we see a collapsed building and a relief tent.
en: News of a great earthquake comes on TV. The screen shows collapsed buildings and relief tents.

ko: 엄마가 피아노 학원에 보내려 합니다. 학원 앞에는 색 바랜 간판이 걸려 있습니다.
mt: My mom's going to send it to a piano school, and in front of it is a colored plate.
en: Mom wants to send you to piano lessons. A faded sign hangs in front of the academy.

ko: 처음으로 거짓말을 했습니다. 엄마가 눈치챈 것 같습니다.
mt: I lied for the first time. I think she noticed.
en: You tell your first lie. Mom seems to have noticed.

ko: 용인 자연농원에서 길을 잃었습니다. 사람들이 밀려다니고 풍선 장수가 소리칩니다.
mt: I'm lost in a natural garden where people are being pushed around, and I'm screaming at the balloon.
en: You get lost at Yongin Farmland. Crowds surge past, and a balloon seller shouts.

ko: 86 아시안게임 열기 속에 유치원 달리기 시합이 열립니다. 운동장 흙먼지가 날립니다.
mt: 86 Asian games open, and there's a kindergarten run-up, and there's dirt on the playground.
en: Amid the 1986 Asian Games fever, the kindergarten holds a footrace. Dust rises from the field.

ko: 집 앞에 버려진 강아지가 있습니다. 강아지는 젖은 눈으로 올려다봅니다.
mt: There's an abandoned puppy in front of the house, and it looks up with a wet eye.
en: An abandoned puppy sits outside your house, looking up at you with wet eyes.

ko: 할아버지 댁 다락방에서 낡은 상자를 발견했습니다. 상자에는 빛바랜 신문지가 덮여 있습니다.
mt: I found an old box in the attic of my grandfather's house, and it's covered with a bright newspaper.
en: In the attic at your grandfather's house, you find an old box covered in yellowed newspaper.

ko: 친구가 당신에게 비밀을 털어놓았습니다. 운동장 뒤편 벤치입니다.
mt: A friend of mine has revealed a secret to you, a bench behind the field.
en: A friend confides a secret to you on the bench behind the schoolyard.

ko: 엄마가 처음으로 심부름을 시켰습니다. 가게까지는 골목을 두 번 돌아야 합니다.
mt: My mom gave me my first errand. I had to go around the alley twice.
en: Mom sends you on your first errand. The shop is two turns down the alley.

ko: 국민학교 입학을 앞두고 있습니다. 엄마가 새 책가방을 사 왔습니다.
mt: I'm getting into elementary school. My mom bought me a new book bag.
en: You are about to start elementary school. Mom brings home a new school bag.

ko: 1987년 국민학교 첫 시험입니다. 책상 위에는 몽당연필 한 자루가 전부입니다.
mt: It's the first exam of the elementary school in 1987, and there's only one bag on top of the desk.
en: 1987, your first elementary school exam. All you have on your desk is a stubby pencil.

ko: 반장 선거가 열립니다. 교실 칠판에는 후보들의 이름이 적혀 있습니다.
mt: There's a class election. The board has the names of the candidates on it.
en: The class president election is held. The candidates' names are written on the board.

ko: 체육 시간 피구 경기입니다. 운동장 바닥에는 흰 분필로 선이 그어져 있습니다.
mt: It's a gym-time ball game, and on the bottom of the field is a line drawn with white chalk.
en: Dodgeball in gym class. Lines are drawn in white chalk on the field.

ko: 학교 앞 문방구에서 뽑기를 합니다. 뽑기 통에는 색색의 종이가 들어 있습니다.
mt: I'm picking it out of the front door of the school, and it's got colored paper in the canister.
en: You try a lucky draw at the stationery shop by the school. The box is full of colored slips.

ko: 담임 선생님이 당신을 따로 부릅니다. 교무실 창문 너머로 운동장이 보입니다.
mt: The teacher calls you separately, and you see the field across the window of the office.
en: Your homeroom teacher calls you aside. The schoolyard is visible through the staff room window.

ko: 교회 여름 성경학교에 참가했습니다. 강당에는 선풍기 세 대가 돌아갑니다.
mt: I attended a summer church Bible school, and there are three fans in the auditorium.
en: You attend the church's summer Bible school. Three fans turn in the hall.

ko: 친구들이 당신을 따돌리려 합니다. 쉬는 시간 교실이 술렁입니다.
mt: Your friends are trying to turn you away. The break is in the classroom.
en: Your classmates try to shut you out. The classroom buzzes during break.

ko: 집에 처음으로 컴퓨터가 생겼습니다. 거실 책상 위에 초록 글씨가 뜨는 모니터가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: And for the first time, there was a computer in the house, and there was a screen with green letters on the living room desk.
en: Your family gets its first computer. A monitor with green text sits on the living room desk.

ko: 할아버지가 돌아가셨습니다. 집안에는 향냄새와 곡소리가 가득합니다.
mt: My grandfather is dead. The house is full of aromas and songs.
en: Your grandfather passes away. The house fills with incense and wailing.

ko: 친구들 사이에서 딱지치기와 만화 스티커 모으기가 유행합니다. 문방구 앞이 북적입니다.
mt: It's popular among my friends to put on a ticker and a comic sticker, and it's crowded in front of the door.
en: Ttakji and cartoon sticker collecting are all the rage. The stationery shop is crowded.

ko: 학교 대표로 글짓기 대회에 나갑니다. 원고지 칸이 빼곡합니다.
mt: I'm going to the school's writing competition, and I'm going to the plaintiff Khan.
en: You represent your school in a writing contest. The manuscript paper grid is dense.

ko: 수영장에서 처음 깊은 물에 들어갑니다. 물빛이 푸르게 출렁입니다.
mt: It's the first deep water in the pool, and the water's blue.
en: You enter deep water for the first time at the pool. The blue water ripples.

ko: 엄마 지갑에서 지폐 한 장이 삐져나와 있습니다. 부엌에서 엄마가 저녁을 짓고 있습니다.
mt: There's a piece of paper out of her purse, and she's making dinner in the kitchen.
en: A bill is sticking out of Mom's wallet. She is making dinner in the kitchen.

ko: 반에 전학생이 왔습니다. 낯선 억양의 말투가 교실에 어색하게 퍼집니다.
mt: There's an awkward spread of strange accents in the classroom.
en: A transfer student joins your class. An unfamiliar accent spreads awkwardly through the room.

ko: 자연 관찰 숙제가 나왔습니다. 공책에는 아직 아무것도 적혀 있지 않습니다.
mt: There's a nature-watching homework. There's nothing in the notebook yet.
en: You are assigned a nature observation project. Your notebook is still blank.

ko: 동네 형이 담배를 권합니다. 골목 모퉁이에는 빈 맥주병이 굴러다닙니다.
mt: My local brother recommends smoking, and there's an empty beer bottle in the corner of the alley.
en: An older neighborhood kid offers you a cigarette. Empty beer bottles roll at the corner.

ko: 친구 생일 선물을 사야 합니다. 용돈은 얼마 남지 않았습니다.
mt: You have to buy a friend's birthday present.
en: You need to buy a friend a birthday present. Your allowance is nearly gone.

ko: 1988년 서울 올림픽 열기 속 가을 운동회, 계주 마지막 주자가 되었습니다. 운동장에 호돌이 깃발이 펄럭입니다.
mt: I became the last runner in the fall of the Olympics in Seoul in 1988.
en: 1988, Seoul Olympics fever. At the autumn sports day, you are the anchor of the relay. Hodori flags flutter over the field.

ko: 꿈속에 하얀 옷을 입은 사람이 나타났습니다. 그 사람의 얼굴은 흐릿합니다.
mt: In a dream, a man in white clothes appears, and his face is blurry.
en: A person in white appears in your dream. Their face is a blur.

ko: 아빠가 사업에 성공해 새로 지은 아파트로 이사했습니다. 현관에는 처음 보는 대리석이 깔려 있습니다.
mt: I moved to my new apartment, where I had my dad's business success, and I had my first marble on the porch.
en: Your father's business takes off, and you move into a new apartment. Marble you have never seen before lines the entrance.

ko: 수학 경시대회 문제를 풉니다. 문제지 여백에는 연습 계산이 가득합니다.
mt: Problem is, the margins are full of practice calculations.
en: You work on a math competition. The margins are full of scratch calculations.

ko: 친구 집에서 처음으로 자고 오게 되었습니다. 친구 집 거실에는 커다란 전축이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: I went to sleep in my friend's house for the first time, and there's a big electric front in my friend's living room.
en: You sleep over at a friend's house for the first time. A big stereo system stands in their living room.

ko: 길거리에서 노숙인이 손을 내밉니다. 찬바람이 불고 있습니다.
mt: There's a homeless man on the street opening his hand. There's a cold wind.
en: A homeless man holds out his hand on the street. A cold wind is blowing.

ko: 담임 선생님이 당신을 편애합니다. 친구들이 수군대기 시작합니다.
mt: The teacher favors you. Friends are starting to work.
en: Your homeroom teacher plays favorites with you. Your classmates start whispering.

ko: 처음으로 혼자 버스를 타고 먼 곳에 가 봅니다. 손에는 버스 회수권 한 장이 쥐어져 있습니다.
mt: For the first time, I'm going to take a bus to a remote location, and I have a bus return in my hand.
en: You take a bus somewhere far on your own for the first time, a bus token clutched in your hand.

ko: 학교 연극에서 악역을 맡았습니다. 무대 위 조명이 뜨겁습니다.
mt: I played the role in the school theater, and the lights on the stage are hot.
en: You are cast as the villain in the school play. The stage lights are hot.

ko: 키가 반에서 가장 작습니다. 아이들이 키 순서로 줄을 설 때마다 맨 앞입니다.
mt: They're the smallest in half, and they're at the front of each key line.
en: You are the shortest in your class. Whenever kids line up by height, you are first.

ko: 친구가 시험지를 보여 달라고 합니다. 시험 시간이 얼마 남지 않았습니다.
mt: A friend of mine asked me to show you the test paper, and I didn't have much time.
en: A friend asks to copy your test. Time is almost up.

ko: 성당 복사단에 들어오라는 권유를 받았습니다. 주일 아침마다 참석해야 합니다.
mt: I was invited to join the church's altar, and I had to attend every morning.
en: You are invited to join the altar servers. You would have to attend every Sunday morning.

ko: 반에서 돈이 없어지는 사건이 일어났습니다. 교실 뒷문은 열려 있습니다.
mt: The back door of the classroom is open.
en: Money goes missing in your class. The back door of the classroom is open.

ko: 가족 여행으로 바닷가에 갔습니다. 바다 냄새가 짭조름합니다.
mt: I went to the beach for my family's trip, and the sea stinks.
en: Your family takes a trip to the seaside. The air tastes of salt.

ko: 학원을 하나 더 다니라는 말을 들었습니다. 가방에는 이미 문제집이 가득합니다.
mt: I've been told to go to one more school, and the bag is already full of problems.
en: You are told to attend one more cram school. Your bag is already full of workbooks.

ko: 친구가 키우던 햄스터가 죽었습니다. 친구는 상자를 끌어안고 울고 있습니다.
mt: A friend of mine, a hamster, is dead, and he's holding his box and crying.
en: A friend's hamster dies. Your friend clutches the box, crying.

ko: 동네 축구팀에서 입단 제의를 받았습니다. 운동장에는 아이들이 공을 차고 있습니다.
mt: I've been asked to join the local football team, and I've got kids wearing balls on the playground.
en: The neighborhood soccer team invites you to join. Kids are kicking a ball on the field.

ko: 부모님 결혼기념일입니다. 식탁에는 평소보다 반찬이 많습니다.
mt: It's my parents' anniversary.
en: It is your parents' wedding anniversary. There are more side dishes on the table than usual.

ko: 오래된 절에서 스님이 차를 대접합니다. 방 안에는 향이 은은하게 피어납니다.
mt: In an old verse, the monk serves the car, and inside the room there is a silvery smell.
en: A monk at an old temple serves you tea. Incense drifts softly through the room.

ko: 처음으로 누군가를 좋아하게 되었습니다. 교실 창가 자리에서 자꾸 그 사람을 봅니다.
mt: For the first time, I've come to love someone, and I keep seeing him in the classroom window.
en: You have a crush for the first time. From your window seat, you keep glancing at them.

ko: 반 대표로 교내 토론 대회에 나갔습니다. 강당에는 선생님들이 앉아 있습니다.
mt: I went to the school debate, as a representative, and there are teachers sitting in the auditorium.
en: You represent your class in the school debate contest. Teachers are seated in the hall.

ko: 집에 도둑이 들었습니다. 현관 자물쇠가 부서져 있습니다.
mt: There's a burglar in the house. The door lock is broken.
en: Your house is burgled. The front door lock is smashed.

ko: 점심시간, 도시락 뚜껑을 여니 좋아하는 분홍 소시지 반찬이 들어 있습니다. 친구들이 젓가락을 들고 몰려듭니다.
mt: At lunchtime, there's a pink sausage breakfast with an open lunch lid, and my friends come in with their chopsticks.
en: Lunchtime. You open your lunchbox to find your favorite pink sausage. Friends swarm in with chopsticks.

ko: 1989년 주가가 천 포인트를 넘었다며 아빠가 주식 이야기를 해 줍니다. 신문 경제면이 식탁 위에 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: My dad tells me about the stock market in 1989 when the stock price was over 1,000 points, and the newspaper economy is on the table.
en: 1989. The stock index has passed 1,000, your father says, and tells you about stocks. The business section is spread across the table.

ko: 반 친구가 괴롭힘을 당하고 있습니다. 쉬는 시간 뒷문 앞에서 소리가 납니다.
mt: My classmates are being harassed, and the sound comes from the back door of the break.
en: A classmate is being bullied. Noise comes from the back door during break.

ko: 동네 도서관에 처음 회원 가입을 했습니다. 도서관 카드가 손에 쥐어집니다.
mt: I was the first member of the local library to have a library card in my hand.
en: You sign up at the neighborhood library for the first time. A library card is placed in your hand.

ko: 독감이 유행합니다. 당신도 걸렸습니다. 방 안에는 약 냄새가 가득합니다.
mt: The flu is epidemic. You've got it, too. There's a lot of medicine in the room.
en: The flu is going around, and you catch it. The room reeks of medicine.

ko: 학교에서 저축의 날 행사가 열렸습니다. 교실 앞 저금통이 점점 무거워집니다.
mt: The day of savings was held at school, and the money in front of the classroom was getting heavier and heavier.
en: The school holds a Savings Day event. The piggy bank at the front of the class grows heavier.

ko: 친한 친구가 이사를 갑니다. 이삿짐 트럭이 골목 앞에 서 있습니다.
mt: My best friend is moving out, and the truck is standing in the alley.
en: Your best friend is moving away. A moving truck waits at the alley.

ko: 부모님의 대화를 엿들었습니다. 집안 형편이 어렵다고 합니다.
mt: I overheard my parents talking, and they said it was hard for the house.
en: You overhear your parents. The family is struggling financially.

ko: 미술 대회에서 상을 받았습니다. 상장과 함께 물감 세트를 받았습니다.
mt: I won a prize at an art competition, and I got a set of paints with my boss.
en: You win a prize in an art contest: a certificate and a set of paints.

ko: 처음으로 친구와 크게 싸웠습니다. 쉬는 시간 운동장 한쪽이 소란스럽습니다.
mt: For the first time, I had a big fight with a friend.
en: You have your first real fight with a friend. A corner of the schoolyard is in an uproar.

ko: 할머니가 집안 대대로 내려오는 이야기를 들려줍니다. 장롱 속 낡은 보자기가 보입니다.
mt: My grandmother tells me stories that come down through the house, and I see an old bloke in the long run.
en: Your grandmother tells you a story handed down through the family. An old cloth bundle is visible in the wardrobe.

ko: 학교에 마술사가 공연을 왔습니다. 강당 불빛이 어둑해집니다.
mt: A magician came to the school, and the hall lights went down.
en: A magician comes to perform at school. The lights in the hall dim.

ko: 체력장 오래달리기를 합니다. 운동장 트랙에 먼지가 일어납니다.
mt: You're running for a long time. Dust is happening on the track of the stadium.
en: The long-distance run for the fitness test. Dust rises from the track.

ko: 처음으로 가족 몰래 새벽 기도에 가 봅니다. 교회 종은 아직 울리지 않았습니다.
mt: The church bell hasn't rang yet.
en: You secretly go to dawn prayer for the first time. The church bell has not yet rung.

ko: 1992년 국민학교 졸업식입니다. 운동장 한쪽에서 꽃다발을 파는 아줌마가 보입니다.
mt: It's 1992 National School graduation, and you see a lady selling flowers on one side of the stadium.
en: 1992, elementary school graduation. A woman is selling bouquets at the edge of the schoolyard.

ko: 부모님이 이혼을 고민한다는 사실을 알게 되었습니다. 밤마다 방문 너머로 낮은 목소리가 들립니다.
mt: I found out that my parents were thinking about getting a divorce, and every night I hear a low voice after a visit.
en: You learn your parents are considering divorce. Every night, low voices drift through the door.

ko: 1993년 중학교 첫 등교입니다. 교복이 어색하고 빳빳합니다.
mt: This is my first year in middle school in 1993, and my uniform is awkward and stiff.
en: 1993, your first day of middle school. Your uniform feels stiff and strange.

mt: Puberty has come. Everything is annoying.
en: Puberty arrives. Everything is irritating.

ko: 거울 속 얼굴에 여드름이 났습니다. 세면대 위에는 비누 하나뿐입니다.
mt: There's acne in the mirror. There's only one soap on top of the sink.
en: A pimple has appeared on your face in the mirror. There is only a bar of soap on the sink.

ko: 중간고사 기간입니다. 교무실 앞 게시판에는 시간표가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: It's a mid-term period. The board in front of the office has a timetable.
en: Midterm exams. The schedule is posted on the board outside the staff room.

ko: 같은 반 친구에게 고백을 받았습니다. 교실 뒤편에서 떨리는 목소리가 들립니다.
mt: I was confessed to by my classmates, and I heard a shaking voice behind the classroom.
en: A classmate confesses their feelings to you. A trembling voice comes from the back of the classroom.

ko: 학교 축제에서 서태지와 아이들 노래로 밴드를 하자는 제안을 받았습니다. 낡은 앰프가 찌직거립니다.
mt: At a school festival, I was offered a band of circuses and children's songs, and the old amps are sore.
en: Someone suggests forming a band for the school festival to play Seo Taiji and Boys. An old amp crackles.

ko: 친구가 술을 몰래 가져왔습니다. 골목 뒤 공터에서 병뚜껑이 열립니다.
mt: A friend steals a drink, and the bottle covers open in the back of the alley.
en: A friend sneaks in some alcohol. A bottle cap pops in the empty lot behind the alley.

ko: 교회 청소년부 수련회에 갔습니다. 캠프 텐트 사이로 밤안개가 깔립니다.
mt: I went to a church youth school, and there was a mist all over the camp tent.
en: You go on the church youth retreat. Night fog settles between the tents.

ko: 모은 용돈으로 무언가를 사려고 합니다. 전자상가 진열대에 워크맨이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: We're going to buy something out of our allowance money, and we're going to have a workman sitting in an electronic shelf.
en: You want to buy something with your saved allowance. A Walkman sits on a shelf at the electronics market.

ko: 학교 불량배가 당신에게 돈을 요구합니다. 체육관 뒤편에는 아무도 없습니다.
mt: The school bully asks you for money. Nobody's behind the gym.
en: A school bully demands money from you. No one is behind the gym.

ko: 진로 상담 시간입니다. 상담실 책상에는 학교 안내책자가 쌓여 있습니다.
mt: It's time for an actual counseling session, and there's a stack of school guides on the table.
en: Career counseling. School brochures are stacked on the counselor's desk.

ko: 반에 다이어트가 유행합니다. 쉬는 시간마다 도시락 얘기가 오갑니다.
mt: It's like half a diet. Every break is about lunch.
en: Dieting is all the rage in your class. Every break is all about lunchboxes.

ko: 같은 반 친구가 몹시 힘들어 보입니다. 교실 창가에서 혼자 울고 있습니다.
mt: The same half of them are crying alone at the window.
en: A classmate looks like they are really struggling, crying alone by the window.

ko: 학교 대표로 과학 경진대회에 나갑니다. 실험실 전등이 밤늦게까지 켜져 있습니다.
mt: I go to a science competition as a school representative, and the lab lights are on late at night.
en: You represent your school at a science fair. The lab lights stay on late into the night.

ko: 체육 시간 철봉 시험입니다. 운동장 철봉에 아이들이 줄을 서 있습니다.
mt: This is a gym-time steel test, and there's a line of kids at the stadium.
en: The pull-up bar test in gym. Kids are lined up at the bars.

ko: PC통신 게시판에서 휴거 소동을 일으켰던 종교 단체에 관한 글을 보게 되었습니다. 전화 모뎀이 삐익거립니다.
mt: I read on the PC news board about a religious organization that caused a break-up, and my phone modem is fumbled.
en: On a PC network board, you read about the religious group behind the Rapture panic. The dial-up modem shrieks.

ko: 반 친구들이 당신을 따라 행동하기 시작합니다. 쉬는 시간마다 당신 주변에 모여듭니다.
mt: My classmates start to act on you, and every break they take, they gather around you.
en: Your classmates start copying what you do. They gather around you every break.

ko: 할머니가 위독하십니다. 병원 복도 끝에서 어머니가 기도하고 있습니다.
mt: My grandmother's dying. She's praying at the end of the hallway.
en: Your grandmother is critically ill. At the end of the hospital hallway, your mother is praying.

ko: 아르바이트를 해 보고 싶습니다. 골목 전봇대에 구인 광고가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: I'd like to do part-time work, and I've got a sign on the alley pole.
en: You want to try a part-time job. A help-wanted ad is stuck to a utility pole in the alley.

ko: 경주로 수학여행을 떠났습니다. 버스 안에서 노래 소리가 흘러나옵니다.
mt: I went on a class trip in a race, and there's a song coming out of the bus.
en: You go on a school trip to Gyeongju. Singing fills the bus.

ko: 짝사랑하던 사람에게 애인이 생겼습니다. 교실 게시판에 두 사람의 사진이 붙어 있습니다.
mt: I have a boyfriend with a lover, and I have two photos on my classroom board.
en: Your crush now has a partner. A photo of the two of them is pinned to the class board.

ko: 학생회 선거에 출마했습니다. 교실 게시판에 후보 포스터가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: I ran for student-election elections with a candidate poster on the classroom board.
en: You run in the student council election. Candidate posters line the class board.

ko: 부모님과 진학 문제로 다툽니다. 식탁 위 밥이 식어 갑니다.
mt: I'm having trouble getting into school with my parents, and the rice cools off on the table.
en: You argue with your parents about school plans. The rice on the table goes cold.

ko: 길에서 현금이 두둑한 지갑을 주웠습니다. 지갑 안에는 명함이 들어 있습니다.
mt: I picked up a big cash wallet on the street, and it's got a card in it.
en: You find a wallet stuffed with cash on the street. There is a business card inside.

ko: 친구가 당신에게 돈을 빌려 달라고 합니다. 교실 창가에서 친구가 머뭇거립니다.
mt: A friend of mine asks you to lend him money.
en: A friend asks to borrow money. They hesitate by the classroom window.

ko: 교회 성가대에서 독창 기회가 왔습니다. 성가대 연습실 피아노 소리가 울립니다.
mt: I've got a solo opportunity at the church choir, and the music plays in the choir room.
en: You get a chance to sing a solo in the church choir. Piano echoes in the rehearsal room.

ko: 늦은 밤 집에 돌아오다 이상한 빛을 보았습니다. 골목 끝 빈 공터가 환합니다.
mt: I came home late at night, and I saw a strange light, and there was an empty space at the end of the alley.
en: Coming home late at night, you see a strange light. The empty lot at the end of the alley is glowing.

ko: 학교 폭력 사건의 목격자가 되었습니다. 복도 끝에서 소란이 일어납니다.
mt: There's an uproar at the end of the hall.
en: You witness a school violence incident. A commotion breaks out at the end of the hall.

ko: 사진부에 들어갔습니다. 암실에서 현상액 냄새가 납니다.
mt: I'm in the photography department, and I smell the fluid in the darkroom.
en: You join the photography club. The darkroom smells of developer.

ko: 친척 모임에서 사촌들과 비교를 당합니다. 명절 마루에 음식이 가득합니다.
mt: You're compared to your cousins at a fraternity. There's plenty of food on the floor of the holidays.
en: At a family gathering, you are compared to your cousins. The holiday floor is covered with food.

ko: 당신이 쓴 글이 신문 독자란에 실려 크게 화제가 되었습니다. 전화기가 쉴 새 없이 울립니다.
mt: Your writing became a big topic for newspaper readerships, and the phone rings all the time.
en: Something you wrote is printed in the newspaper's letters section and causes a stir. The phone won't stop ringing.

ko: 몸이 자주 아파 병원을 찾습니다. 진료실에는 소독약 냄새가 납니다.
mt: He's sick a lot. He's looking for a hospital.
en: You get sick often and keep visiting the hospital. The exam room smells of disinfectant.

ko: 친구들과 노래방에 갔습니다. 번쩍이는 조명 아래 탬버린이 놓여 있습니다.
mt: I went to the singing hall with my friends, and there's a tambourine under the flashing lights.
en: You go to a karaoke room with friends. A tambourine lies beneath the flashing lights.

ko: 아빠가 회사 일로 큰 빚을 졌습니다. 집 앞에는 낯선 사람들이 드나듭니다.
mt: He's deeply in debt for the company, and there's strangers in front of the house.
en: Your father takes on a huge debt through his company. Strangers come and go at your door.

ko: 학교 도서관 구석에서 금서로 분류된 책을 발견했습니다. 표지가 낡고 누렇습니다.
mt: I found a book in the corner of the school library, with a long, dark cover.
en: In a corner of the school library, you find a book classified as banned. Its cover is worn and yellowed.

ko: 체육 대회 줄다리기에서 반이 졌습니다. 운동장 흙바닥에 줄이 끊어져 있습니다.
mt: I've lost half of my gym bridge, and the lines are cut off on the dirt floor of the stadium.
en: Your class loses the tug-of-war at sports day. The broken rope lies on the dirt field.

ko: 길거리에서 전도하는 사람들을 만났습니다. 하얀 전단지가 바람에 날립니다.
mt: I met people preaching on the streets, white flyers flying in the wind.
en: You run into street evangelists. White flyers flutter in the wind.

ko: 첫 데이트를 하게 되었습니다. 약속 장소는 시내 햄버거 가게입니다.
mt: I got my first date. The appointment place is a city hamburger shop.
en: You go on your first date. You are meeting at a burger place downtown.

ko: 동네 오락실에서 누군가 격투 게임 내기를 걸어 옵니다. 오락기 화면이 번쩍입니다.
mt: There's somebody in the local entertainment room who's walking into a fight game, and there's a flash.
en: At the neighborhood arcade, someone challenges you to a bet on a fighting game. The screen flashes.

ko: 중학교 졸업을 앞두고 있습니다. 교실 칠판에는 졸업 축하 글이 적혀 있습니다.
mt: I'm about to graduate from middle school.
en: Middle school graduation is near. Congratulations are written on the blackboard.

ko: 1996년 고등학교 입학식입니다. 운동장 스피커에서 교가가 흘러나옵니다.
mt: This is the 1996 high school entrance school, and there's a teacher coming out of the stadium speaker.
en: 1996, the high school entrance ceremony. The school song blares from the speakers on the field.

ko: 야간 자율 학습 시간입니다. 교실 형광등이 웅웅거립니다.
mt: It's the time of night autonomy learning. Classlights are ringing.
en: Evening self-study hall. The fluorescent lights hum.

ko: 처음으로 철학 수업을 들었습니다. 칠판에 낯선 외국 이름이 적혀 있습니다.
mt: For the first time, I took a philosophy class, and the blackboard had a strange foreign name on it.
en: You attend your first philosophy class. Unfamiliar foreign names are written on the board.

ko: 연인이 생겼습니다. 삐삐에 둘만 아는 숫자 암호가 찍힙니다.
mt: We've got a lover. We've got two numbers on the page.
en: You have a sweetheart. A numeric code only the two of you know flashes on your pager.

ko: 모의고사 성적표가 나왔습니다. 교실 복도에 성적 순위표가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: There's a mocker's report card, and there's a rating card in the hallway.
en: Your mock exam results are out. Rankings are posted in the hallway.

ko: 동네 교회에서 청년부 리더를 제안받았습니다. 교회 마당에 은행나무가 노랗게 물들었습니다.
mt: I was offered a young leader at a local church, and the bank tree was yellow in the church yard.
en: You are offered a youth group leader role at the neighborhood church. The ginkgo tree in the churchyard has turned gold.

ko: 운동부 코치가 당신에게 선수 생활을 권합니다. 운동장 트랙이 빗물에 젖어 있습니다.
mt: A sports coach invites you to play. The track is wet with rainwater.
en: A sports coach urges you to become an athlete. The track is wet with rain.

ko: 친구가 함께 가출하자고 합니다. 역 대합실 시계가 밤 열한 시를 가리킵니다.
mt: A friend of mine says, "Let's run away together." The station watch points to the 11th hour of the night.
en: A friend suggests running away together. The clock in the station waiting room reads eleven at night.

ko: 첫 아르바이트 월급을 받았습니다. 봉투 안에는 빳빳한 지폐가 들어 있습니다.
mt: I got my first part-time salary.
en: You receive your first part-time paycheck. The envelope holds crisp bills.

ko: 교내에 당신에 대한 나쁜 소문이 돕니다. 복도 끝에서 수군거리는 소리가 들립니다.
mt: There's a bad rumor in the school about you. There's a chatter at the end of the hall.
en: Ugly rumors about you spread around school. Whispering echoes from the end of the hall.

ko: 꿈에서 거대한 뱀이 당신을 휘감았습니다. 잠에서 깨어 보니 땀에 젖어 있습니다.
mt: In my dream, a huge snake is enshrining you, and when I wake up, I'm sweating.
en: In a dream, a giant serpent coils around you. You wake drenched in sweat.

ko: 학교에 봉사 활동 점수가 생겼습니다. 수학여행 대신 봉사 활동을 갈 기회가 생겼습니다.
mt: I had a volunteer activity score in my school, and I had an opportunity to go out and do it instead of doing class trips.
en: The school introduces volunteer credits. You get a chance to do volunteer work instead of the school trip.

ko: 같은 성별의 친한 친구가 당신에게 사랑을 고백했습니다. 교정 벤치에 두 사람만 앉아 있습니다.
mt: A close friend of the same sex has confessed to you, and only two people are sitting on the campus bench.
en: A close friend of the same sex confesses their love to you. The two of you sit alone on a campus bench.

ko: 학교 축제 무대에서 연설을 하게 되었습니다. 무대 조명이 강하게 쏟아집니다.
mt: I was given a speech on a school festival stage, and there was a lot of light on the stage.
en: You are to give a speech on stage at the school festival. The stage lights pour down hard.

ko: 처음으로 술자리에 참석했습니다. 포장마차 안에는 소주병이 줄지어 있습니다.
mt: For the first time, I went to the bar, and there's a line of soju bottles in the cart.
en: You attend your first drinking session. Soju bottles line up in the street tent bar.

ko: 수능을 백일 앞두고 있습니다. 책상 위 달력에 동그라미가 가득합니다.
mt: We're a hundred days ahead of us. The calendar on our desk is full of circles.
en: The college entrance exam is a hundred days away. The calendar on your desk is covered in circles.

ko: 친구의 부모님이 사이비 종교에 빠졌다고 합니다. 친구 얼굴에 그늘이 져 있습니다.
mt: His parents are involved in cults. He's got a shadow on his face.
en: A friend says their parents have fallen into a pseudo-religious cult. A shadow hangs over their face.

ko: 길거리 카드 도박판을 지나갑니다. 판 위에는 지폐 뭉치가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: I walk through the street card gambling, and there's a bunch of bills on the board.
en: You pass a street card game. A wad of bills sits on the table.

ko: 신문에 당신의 선행이 실렸습니다. 학교 게시판에 신문 기사가 붙어 있습니다.
mt: You've got your good deeds on the newspaper board. You've got newspaper articles on the school board.
en: Your good deed makes the newspaper. The article is posted on the school board.

ko: 대학 입시 면접장입니다. 면접실 문틈으로 면접관들의 목소리가 새어 나옵니다.
mt: This is a college entrance interview, and the audience's voice comes out through the doors of the interview.
en: A university admissions interview. The interviewers' voices leak through the door.

ko: 부모님이 가업을 이으라고 하십니다. 가게 장부가 식탁 위에 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: My parents tell me to do a family business, and the store book is spread out on the table.
en: Your parents want you to take over the family business. The shop ledger lies open on the table.

ko: 몸이 아파 입원하게 되었습니다. 병실 창밖으로 빨래가 바람에 흔들립니다.
mt: I'm sick, and I'm hospitalized, and the laundry is shaken out of the window of the room by the wind.
en: You fall ill and are hospitalized. Laundry sways in the wind outside the ward window.

ko: 독립해서 혼자 살 기회가 생겼습니다. 원룸 창문 너머로 노을이 보입니다.
mt: I have an opportunity to live alone on my own, and I see the oars across the window in the main room.
en: You get a chance to move out and live alone. The sunset glows beyond your studio window.

ko: 자원봉사로 요양원을 찾았습니다. 복도에는 소독약 냄새가 감돕니다.
mt: I found a nursing home volunteer.
en: You volunteer at a nursing home. The smell of disinfectant lingers in the hall.

ko: 친구가 다단계 사업을 권합니다. 카페 테이블에는 설명서가 펼쳐져 있습니다.
mt: A friend of mine recommends a multi-level business, and there's a manual at the cafe table.
en: A friend pitches you a multilevel marketing scheme. Brochures are spread across the café table.

ko: 대학 합격 발표 날입니다. 게시판 앞에 학생들이 빽빽하게 모여 있습니다.
mt: It's the day of the college pass, and there's a bunch of students in front of the board.
en: Admission results day. Students crowd thickly around the bulletin board.

ko: 삼풍백화점 붕괴 소식이 아직 생생한데, 당신도 큰 사고를 당할 뻔했다가 기적적으로 피했습니다. 사고 현장에는 구급차 불빛이 번쩍입니다.
mt: The news of the crash is still vivid, but you're about to have a big accident, and you're miraculously avoiding it, and there's an ambulance light on the scene.
en: The Sampoong Department Store collapse is still fresh in memory when you narrowly, miraculously escape a major accident yourself. Ambulance lights flash at the scene.

ko: IMF 외환위기로 회사에서 밀려난 아버지가 쓰러지셨습니다. 응급실 복도에서 어머니가 울고 있습니다.
mt: My father has collapsed from an IMF externality crisis, and my mother is crying in the E.R. hallway.
en: Pushed out of his company by the IMF crisis, your father collapses. Your mother weeps in the ER hallway.

ko: 당신을 따르는 후배들이 생겼습니다. 동아리방에 후배들이 모여 앉아 있습니다.
mt: There's a boat following you, and they're sitting in the club room.
en: Younger students begin to follow you. They gather in the club room.

ko: 연인과 이별했습니다. 비가 그친 골목 끝에서 우산 하나를 접고 있습니다.
mt: I've been separated from my lover, and I'm folding an umbrella at the end of the alley where the rain has stopped.
en: You break up with your sweetheart. At the end of an alley after the rain, you fold a single umbrella.

ko: 친구들과 밤새 인생에 대해 이야기합니다. 옥상 위에 별이 가득합니다.
mt: I talk about my life all night long, and there's stars on the roof.
en: You talk about life with friends all night. The rooftop sky is full of stars.

ko: 우연히 오래된 종교 의식 서적을 손에 넣었습니다. 표지에 한자가 빼곡하게 적혀 있습니다.
mt: I happen to have an old religious ritual book in my hand, and it's written on the cover with the letters.
en: By chance, you come into possession of an old book of religious rites. Its cover is crowded with Chinese characters.

ko: 새로운 출발을 앞두고 있습니다. 책상 위에는 대학 입학 원서가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: There's a university entrance library on the desk.
en: A new start lies ahead. A university application sits on your desk.

ko: 길에서 쓰러진 노인을 발견했습니다. 주변에는 장바구니가 흩어져 있습니다.
mt: We found an old man who's fallen on the street, and there's a bag basket all around him.
en: You find an old man collapsed in the street. His groceries are scattered around him.

ko: 한 노인이 당신이 큰 무리를 이끌 운명이라고 말합니다. 공원 벤치에서 노인이 담배를 피우고 있습니다.
mt: An old man says you're destined to lead a large crowd, and an old man is smoking a cigarette in a park bench.
en: An old man tells you that you are destined to lead a great multitude. He is smoking on a park bench.

ko: IMF 외환위기로 아르바이트하던 가게에서 월급이 몇 달째 밀렸습니다. 사무실 구석에 서류 더미가 쌓여 있습니다.
mt: The IMF foreign exchange crisis has pushed the salary of a working store for months, and there's a pile of paperwork in the corner of the office.
en: Because of the IMF crisis, the shop where you work part-time has not paid you in months. Stacks of paperwork pile up in the office corner.

ko: 오랜만에 고향 교회를 찾았습니다. 교회 종탑 위에 비둘기가 앉아 있습니다.
mt: After a long time, I found my home church, and there's a pigeon sitting on a church bell tower.
en: You visit your hometown church after a long time. Pigeons sit atop the bell tower.

ko: 사람들이 이상하게 당신의 말에 귀를 기울입니다. 교실에서 친구들이 당신을 바라봅니다.
mt: People are curiously listening to you. They're looking at you in the classroom.
en: People listen to you with strange attention. Your classmates watch you.

ko: 열여덟 번째 생일입니다. 식탁 위 미역국과 케이크가 놓여 있습니다.
mt: It's my 18th birthday.
en: Your eighteenth birthday. Seaweed soup and a cake sit on the table.

ko: 세상에 대한 의문이 깊어집니다. 기존 종교로는 답을 찾을 수 없습니다.
mt: It's a question of the world. We can't find the answer with conventional religion.
en: Your doubts about the world deepen. The established religions hold no answers for you.

mt: I'm trying to flip it again.
en: Wriggle to roll over again

ko: 몇 번이고 버둥거린 끝에 다시 뒤집혔습니다. 어머니가 웃음을 터뜨립니다.
mt: And after a couple of clumsiness, she turned it over, and she laughed.
en: After wriggling again and again, you roll over once more. Your mother bursts out laughing.

ko: 힘이 빠져 엎어진 채 한참을 울었습니다.
mt: I cried for a long time when I was so weak that I fell down.
en: Your strength gives out, and you cry facedown for a long time.

mt: She smiles at you.
en: Beam at Mom

ko: 방긋 웃어 보이자 옆집 아주머니까지 달려와 감탄했습니다.
mt: And when I looked at her smile, she ran up to her neighbor's wife and she was amazed.
en: You flash a smile, and even the neighbor lady rushes over to marvel.

mt: I can't sleep.
en: Fall asleep as you are

mt: As soon as I was full, I fell asleep.
en: With a full belly, you drift off in no time.

mt: I'm amazed at the sound of your hand claps.
en: Cry at the sound of clapping

ko: 놀란 울음은 곧 젖을 물고 잦아들었습니다.
mt: I was amazed and cried, and soon I was wet and wet and wet.
en: Your startled crying soon fades at the breast.

ko: 손뼉 소리에 놀라 더 크게 울음을 터뜨렸습니다.
mt: I was surprised by the applause, and I cried louder.
en: Startled by the clapping, you wail even louder.

mt: She cries out loud. She asks for milk.
en: Cry loudly for milk

mt: She cries, and she quickly bites her milk.
en: At your cries, your mother hurriedly nurses you.

ko: 울다 지친 어머니가 한숨을 쉬며 달래는 소리에 잠이 듭니다.
mt: My mother, tired of crying, goes to sleep with a sigh of relief.
en: Exhausted by your crying, your mother sighs and soothes you, and you fall asleep.

mt: You suck your fingers and you hold them.
en: Suck your fingers and hold out

ko: 손가락을 빨며 꾹 참자 어머니가 쪽잠을 청할 수 있었습니다.
mt: She could suck her fingers and she could ask for a nap.
en: You suck your fingers and hold out, letting your mother catch a short nap.

mt: They call out to their parents.
en: Babble for your parents

ko: 옹알이에 부모가 화답하며 방 안이 따뜻해집니다.
mt: The parents respond and the room warms up.
en: Your parents babble back, and the room grows warm.

ko: 옹알이를 알아듣지 못한 부모는 피곤한 얼굴로 돌아눕습니다.
mt: The parent who doesn't understand the angst turns tired.
en: Not understanding your babbling, your parents roll over with tired faces.

mt: I'm looking at something in the dark.
en: Stare quietly at something in the dark

ko: 어둠 속 희미한 빛에 마음이 이상하게 편안해집니다.
mt: The faint light in the dark makes me feel strangely comfortable.
en: A faint light in the dark brings you a strange calm.

ko: 어둠 속 그림자가 무서워 울음이 터집니다.
mt: The shadows in the dark start to scare me, and I burst into tears.
en: The shadows in the dark frighten you, and you burst into tears.

mt: You look like you're smiling.
en: Smile brightly

mt: They're happy and they're going to give you candy.
en: The delighted guest presses a candy into your hand.

mt: I'm gonna cry. I'm gonna cry. I'm gonna cry.
en: Scream and cry

ko: 울음소리에 손님이 당황해 얼른 안겨 줄 사람을 찾습니다.
mt: I'm just looking for someone to give me a quick hug because I'm embarrassed by the sound.
en: Flustered by your crying, the guest hurriedly looks for someone to hand you to.

ko: 울음소리에 집 안이 시끄러워져 손님이 서둘러 떠납니다.
mt: The sound of the house is so loud that the guest leaves in a hurry.
en: Your crying fills the house, and the guest leaves in a hurry.

mt: I'm holding on to your shiny ring.
en: Grab the guest's shiny ring

ko: 반지를 움켜쥔 손을 떼지 않자 손님은 웃으며 반지를 빼 줍니다.
mt: When you don't take your hand off the ring, the customer laughs and removes the ring.
en: You won't let go of the ring, so the guest laughs and slips it off for you.

mt: He grabs the ring, and he gets upset with the guest.
en: You grab the ring and get scolded by the guest.

mt: I'm just gonna stare at your eyes.
en: Stare quietly into the guest's eyes

ko: 손님은 아이의 눈빛에 마음이 흔들린 듯 말없이 웃습니다.
mt: The customer laughs silently, as if his eyes were shaking.
en: Moved by the child's gaze, the guest smiles without a word.

mt: They turn their heads in embarrassment.
en: The guest looks away, embarrassed.

mt: Paper money.
en: Banknote

ko: 지폐를 잡자 온 가족이 부자가 될 거라며 환호합니다.
mt: When we grab the bills, we cheer that the whole family is going to be rich.
en: You grab the banknote, and the whole family cheers that you will be rich.

ko: 지폐가 찢어져 손에 쥔 것은 반쪽뿐입니다.
mt: It's only half of the money that's been torn apart.
